quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 results (CFO Steve Litchfield): total revenue was $218.1 million, up 29% from $168.8 million in the previous quarter and up 72% from $126.5 million in the third quarter of 2025; infrastructure revenue grew to approximately $125 million, broadband approximately $53 million, connectivity approximately $25 million and industrial and multi-market approximately $15 million. GAAP and non-GAAP gross margin were 58.7% and 60%; GAAP operating expenses $97.8 million and non-GAAP $66.5 million; GAAP operating margin 13.9% and non-GAAP operating margin 29.5%; GAAP diluted EPS 30 cents and non-GAAP 62 cents. Net cash used in operating activities was approximately 13.6 million; MaxLinear exited Q3 with approximately $109.9 million in cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash, which included a substantial wafer prepayment (rendered 'waivers' in the transcript) supporting rising demand for its data center products. Days sales outstanding approximately 31 days versus 28 days; days of inventory down from 123 days to 111 days. CEO Kishore Seendripu: infrastructure 'grew 210% year-on-year' and is 'now larger than the rest of our revenue categories combined'; the AI data-centric business 'continues to outperform our expectations'.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $218.1 million, +72% YoY, +29% QoQ; infrastructure ~$125 million (+210% YoY); non-GAAP gross margin 60%; non-GAAP operating margin 29.5%; non-GAAP EPS 62 cents

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance: CEO Kishore Seendripu said MaxLinear is 'raising our 2026 optical data center revenue outlook to $250 million to $270 million' and, 'With strong visibility in bookings extending beyond 2027, we expect another significant step-up in revenue next year.' Q4 2026 (CFO Steve Litchfield): revenue expected between $240 and $260 million, with strong growth in infrastructure driven by data center optical interconnects, broadband and connectivity down seasonally and industrial multi-market up; GAAP gross margin approximately 58 to 61% and non-GAAP gross margin 59 to 62%; GAAP operating expenses $96 million to $101 million and non-GAAP $65 to $70 million; GAAP and non-GAAP interest and other expense approximately $3.5 to $4.3 million; diluted share count approximately 99.7 million. CFO on 2027: 'I don't think we're planning to give guidance' yet, but 'I would expect to see us outgrow the market in 2027.'
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 optical data center revenue $250 million to $270 million; Q4 2026 revenue $240 to $260 million; Q4 non-GAAP gross margin 59 to 62%

quarterly_data.signal: 1.6T Rushmore timing (CEO Kishore Seendripu): qualification programs for Rushmore-based 200-gigabit per lane PAM4 1.6 terabit architectures are 'advancing toward expected production deployments in 2027'; 'there's an initial design win that will start shipping in the first half', the exact quantities 'not clear, but it's meaningful in the sense that it sets up the second half very nicely', with 'initial revenues actually in early 27 and stronger ramp in the second half'. MaxLinear has 'commitments both for DSP and TIA in these design wins', and looking to '28 and 29, it's going to be a massive growth driver for us', with Keystone at 800 gig still growing. Qualification momentum is accelerating across module makers; the CEO said MaxLinear is 'bottlenecked by our own ability to support multiple' qualifications simultaneously - a constraint of internal resources, 'nothing to do with wafer supply' - so it sequences and prioritizes them. CFO Steve Litchfield: '1.6T starts in 27, but it'll have a much bigger growth year in 2028'; the 2028 mix is 'substantially 1.6, maybe you'll see 800 kind of trailing off, but potentially it can sustain as well up until probably 2029'. Next: Big Sky, the 400-gigabit per lane 3.2 terabit optical and electrical PAM4 interconnect family, which the CEO said 'will further catalyze growth' as speeds go beyond 200-gigabit per lane.
quarterly_data.figure: 1.6T Rushmore initial design win shipping in the first half, initial revenues in early 27, stronger ramp in the second half; bigger growth year in 2028

quarterly_data.signal: Bookings and backlog: CFO Steve Litchfield said MaxLinear has 'committed order backlog throughout 2027' for its data center products and is 'booking products throughout 27 into 2028'; 'lead times for optical product are 26, 28 weeks, but customers are certainly coming in and placing orders out much further than that, just kind of given they want to secure supply', and 'backlog as you would imagine is very, very good in 27 and into 2028'. CEO Kishore Seendripu: 'With strong customer momentum, great backlog visibility'. Separately, the XGS PON hyperscale data center design win, which serves as the control-plane connectivity network across multiple data centers, 'has completed qualification', and 'Supported by secured backlog, we expect first deployments of this inter-data center control plane solution to start in 2027.'
quarterly_data.figure: committed order backlog throughout 2027; bookings into 2028; optical lead times 26, 28 weeks; XGS PON design win first deployments in 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Supply (CEO Kishore Seendripu): 'I think the optic supply is easing. We are really constrained by foundries on the DSP supply. And the data center build-out is really accelerating'; fab capacity 'is not coming online', 'there's really, really a fab capacity shortage', and 'the DSP supply is a pretty strong supply constraint'. In an earlier answer not addressed to a named executive, management said wafer capacities 'are allocated by companies, by the major foundry', each company choosing how to split its 5 nanometer silicon between switch, pluggables, GPUs and TPUs, and that it does not see double ordering: 'nobody's signing real long-term agreements', 'There's a lot of manufacturing shortage', and data center customers keep qualified optics / DSP supply chains unique. The CEO also said MaxLinear's 'supply diversity across the various speed nodes across 800 gig and 1.6 terabit on the supply lines, including the fabrication process' means its product lines do not compete 'for the same technology node'. CFO Steve Litchfield: 'I expect prepaids to continue to go up from here.'
quarterly_data.figure: DSP supply constrained by foundries; optic supply easing; prepaids expected to continue to go up

quarterly_data.signal: Wafer prepayments including TSMC: asked about the rise in prepaid assets and whether the wafers secured support the 2027 backlog, CFO Steve Litchfield said 'the prepayments, mostly on the wafer side' and 'on the balance sheet isn't just TSMC. There's other things on prepayments as well that we don't break out'.

Market share (management): CEO Kishore Seendripu said share is 'very hard to estimate' given accelerating unit demand; looking backward 'we are well above the number' cited in the question, and two years from now 'It should be in the teens for sure'; 'we are gaining share every day. I think in a 12 to 24 window, we could be neck and neck with one of our two competitors. Right? That's the hope, that's the goal'. CFO Steve Litchfield: 'being up in the teens over the next couple of years, very achievable', and management said it is 'very confident we're outgrowing the market'. Customer breadth (CEO): optical revenues are 'quite broad-based. It's across all the major module makers', a growing set of module makers is engaged on 1.6 terabit, the US is 'in a more advanced phase of 1.6 terabit deployments' and will adopt 1.6 terabit 'a much earlier cycle than their Chinese counterparts'; management called MaxLinear 'the only pure-play DSP provider on the optical pluggable'. Keystone, the 5-nanometer CMOS 100-gigabit per lane PAM4 family, 'continues to ramp rapidly in high-volume production across multiple hyperscalers'.
quarterly_data.figure: share 'in the teens' in two years; could be neck and neck with one of two competitors in 12 to 24 months

quarterly_data.signal: Content per port at 1.6T (CEO Kishore Seendripu): the proverbial 2X price step 'historically never stuck when you change speeds', 'But this time it's sticking': 'the ASP on the DSP is more or less doubling and then we have TIA that we did not add before. So all in all, we'll be growing more than a 2X on the ASP number.' Washington TIA attach: 'In the short term, let's say it's an 80% attach rate', about 100% in a year and a half and 'we hope to be more than 100%' because the TIA also works with other DSPs; the CEO said there is 'only one other real TIA vendor that meets the performance benchmarks' for a 1.6 terabit product and MaxLinear hopes 'to be the other guy'.
quarterly_data.figure: DSP ASP more or less doubling at 1.6T, more than 2X with TIA; TIA attach about 80% short term, 100% in a year and a half

quarterly_data.signal: Annapurna and Washington (CEO Kishore Seendripu): Annapurna, the 1.6 terabit electrical interconnect family, addresses 1.6 terabit active electrical cable and onboard retimer applications for AI scale-up; Washington, the 200-gigabit per lane TIA platform, supports DSP-based optics and non-DSP LRO, LPO, NPO and CPO solutions; 'We expect initial Washington and Annapurna revenues in 2027, followed by a stronger volume ramp in 2028.' MaxLinear is also in 'a strong qual cycle on electrical products as well at the 1.6 terabit speeds'. On AECs the CEO described Credo as the one large leader ('93% or maybe 99%' of the AEC market) and said the market is diversifying to multiple AEC vendors; MaxLinear will sell silicon to a cable maker or paddle-card maker at pricing he expects to be similar to its PAM4 DSP for optical, is 'planning around one or two big data centers', and said 'we should be able to get to 20 to 30% in the 1.6 terabyte cycle somewhere in the next couple of years'; 'We only want our two data centers in the US.'
quarterly_data.figure: Washington and Annapurna initial revenues in 2027, stronger ramp in 2028; AEC aim 20 to 30% in the 1.6 terabit cycle

quarterly_data.signal: NPO / CPO view (CEO Kishore Seendripu, 'my personal view. Not a market view'): on a snapshot basis in 2030, 'you should expect 60 to 70 percent pluggable, 20 percent NPO, and 10 percent all various forms of it'. 'CPO has gotten delayed because the challenge of the optics in a hybridized' co-packaged configuration 'is a very huge problem', so NPO, with maintenance, modularity and supplier-diversity advantages, 'will be big'; LRO 'is a real option at the 200 gig per lane' and a major option at 400 gig per lane, while LPOs are 'a very small fraction, point technology'. The CPO opportunity 'really is a scale-up side, which is a greenfield opportunity'; NPO, and CPO at higher speeds, will need a DSP or half DSP. MaxLinear expects to 'be a major player in NPO and LROs' and has TIAs and drivers announced across those categories.
quarterly_data.figure: CEO view for 2030: 60 to 70 percent pluggable, 20 percent NPO, 10 percent other

quarterly_data.signal: AI infrastructure beyond PAM4 (CEO Kishore Seendripu): the AI Rack Commander portfolio of USB, PCIe and UART connectivity bridges for telemetry, power management and protection in rack-scale AI infrastructure 'expands our role beyond data movement and into the control plane of the AI data center', which he believes is 'a significant long-term growth opportunity'. Panther, the storage accelerator platform that raises effective storage utilization and unlocks KV cache capacity for agentic AI: 'We expect Panther revenue to roughly double this year with potential for another meaningful increase in 2027.' Gross margin (CFO Steve Litchfield): up from 58 to 60 percent this quarter with guidance at 60.5, 'despite some of the cost increases' across the ecosystem, 'Some of that we've been able to pass along to the customer', and 'as the mix continues toward more infrastructure products, I think you will see our gross margin continue to trend up.'
quarterly_data.figure: Panther revenue to roughly double this year; non-GAAP gross margin 60 percent, guidance 60.5

quarterly_data.signal: Broadband, connectivity and wireless: both broadband and connectivity grew sequentially in Q3, 'driven by large-scale deployments of fiber PON and Wi-Fi 7 gateways at major Tier 1 service providers in North America and Europe' (CEO Kishore Seendripu). The CEO expects edge AI-driven upgrades to drive growth in 2027 and 2028 for wireless infrastructure and broadband access and connectivity, including the single-chip 5G remote radio unit solution, millimeter-wave and microwave backhaul RF and modem SoCs, and XGS PON fiber broadband home gateways. CFO Steve Litchfield: seasonality in Q4, but from telco spending and 'our market share gains on the' PON side (rendered 'pond' in the transcript), 'we do expect to see growth in 2027'.
